context: Recent work established several adjacent facts that should be fixed and verified together. PR #46 stopped semantic-cache hits from being counted as fresh provider health. Follow-up review found that the current reliability decorator still observes only the final adapter outcome, so intermediate provider fallback failures are invisible. The provider reliability tracker may also admit an open circuit into half-open before the wire adapter executes the fallback; if that recovery fallback is satisfied from semantic cache, no fresh provider result reaches the circuit and the breaker can remain half-open indefinitely because the underlying circuit primitive has no automatic half-open timeout. In addition, Codex tasks 008 and 009 each reported one unrelated local npm-test failure because the executor DNS maps example.com to RFC2544 198.18.0.0/15 and the SSRF guard correctly blocks it. GitHub CI passes, so that test must be made DNS-deterministic without weakening SSRF. PR #52 fixed the rc.1 real-web route lifecycle, so browser count-guard checks that were previously blocked by missing /image-mind/* routes should be retried in this same batch when practical. Existing draft PR #53 on branch fix/per-provider-reliability-probes already contains the first reliability implementation slice and must be preserved and continued rather than duplicated or discarded. Existing draft PR #53 and branch fix/per-provider-reliability-probes remain the execution vehicle for this batch: preserve its existing implementation commits, sync the validated latest main source commit into it non-destructively, push completion back to that branch, and do not merge PR #53 during executor execution.

Preserve retry, model fallback, provider fallback, split, credential-scoped semantic-cache, explicit-provider stickiness, and execution-trace behavior unless this task explicitly tightens reliability semantics.
Make reliability observe each configured provider attempt (primary and every automatic provider fallback) rather than infer intermediate outcomes only from the final result.
A provider-level terminal failure on fallback-1 must update fallback-1 health/circuit even if fallback-2 later succeeds.
A semantic-cache hit must never count as a fresh provider health success.

A half-open recovery probe must perform a real provider attempt and must not be satisfied by semantic cache. Prefer a request-scoped no-store/refresh mechanism over clearing global cache. The recovery probe must still preserve ordinary cache behavior for unrelated providers and requests.

If a half-open recovery probe succeeds, its circuit must close and health success must increment exactly once. If it fails with a provider-level reliability failure, its circuit must return to open and failure accounting must increment exactly once.
Concurrent callers must preserve the existing exactly-one half-open probe guarantee; a second caller must not route another recovery probe while the first is in flight.

Do not double-count provider outcomes. If production accounting moves into the wire adapter/provider-attempt seam, remove or bypass overlapping outer-decorator accounting in the production composition.

Keep aggregate VisionTrace semantics correct across retries and provider fallbacks: providerCalls/retries/cacheHits/modelFallbacks/providerFallbacks/splits must remain truthful and providerFallbacks must count actual alternate provider attempts.

Fix the tool-thin/example.com regression test so it is independent of public DNS and remains fully offline/deterministic. Do not weaken the SSRF implementation or whitelist RFC2544/non-public ranges just to make the test pass. Mock/fixture the DNS or loading seam instead.
Keep all new reliability metadata provider-neutral and free of credentials/endpoints/secrets beyond existing safe provider ids.
All product changes remain within allowed image-mind reliability/adapter/test files; no Harness-owned file is directly edited by project code or executor.
Intermediate automatic provider fallback failures become first-class reliability observations rather than being lost behind the final fallback result.
Half-open recovery cannot be completed from semantic cache and cannot become permanently stuck because of a cache hit; it ends in closed on fresh success or open on fresh provider failure.
Ordinary semantic-cache behavior remains intact and cache hits still never count as fresh health success.
No duplicate health/circuit accounting occurs for a single provider attempt.
Aggregate execution traces remain truthful for provider calls, retries, cache hits, model/provider fallbacks, and splits.
The DNS-dependent tool-thin test is deterministic/offline and full npm test passes in the executor environment; do not classify the known RFC2544 DNS mapping as a product failure after this fix.
Repository typecheck/build/test/package/built checks PASS unless a genuinely new unrelated environment blocker is evidenced; do not hide failures.
